__doc__: How OpenClaw attaches files named by `MEDIA:` lines in the MODEL'S REPLY TEXT, read statically from the published packages openclaw 2026.7.1 (dist/*.js, a local install) and openclaw 2026.9.9 (npm pack, dist/*.mjs), 2026-10-17; the `cases` were evaluated by importing the dists' pure parser and sanitizer functions (reply-directives parseReplyDirectives after sanitizeAssistantVisibleText and, on 2026.9.9, sanitizeUserFacingText), with no agent, no model and no network. Pins interceptors/anthropic-proxy/src/reply-media.ts (openclawMediaRefs, mediaLineState, planReplyMedia) and its tests. Excerpts are the source text, trimmed.

grammar.where: src/media/parse.ts splitMediaFromOutput (2026.7.1, payloads-*.js); src/media/parse-output.ts splitMediaOutput (2026.9.9, parse-output-*.mjs), both called through src/auto-reply/reply/reply-directives.ts parseReplyDirectives
grammar.line: the reply is cut at "\n"; a line is a directive when its first non-blank characters are `MEDIA:` in any case. 2026.9.9: `line.trimStart().slice(0, 6).toUpperCase().startsWith("MEDIA:")`; 2026.7.1: `line.trimStart().toUpperCase().startsWith("MEDIA:")`. trimStart strips every JS whitespace (NBSP, BOM, U+2028 …).
grammar.token: MEDIA_TOKEN_RE = /\bMEDIA:\s*`?([^\n]+)`?/gi: the payload is the rest of the line after the first `MEDIA:` and optional blanks and backtick; one match per line (the capture is greedy)
grammar.payload: a payload wrapped in matching ", ' or ` is ONE reference (spaces allowed). Otherwise it is cut at blanks (2026.7.1 split(/\s+/); 2026.9.9 splitUnquotedMediaDirectiveParts re-joins a run that starts at a path root and has no extension yet, so `/home/u/my file.png` is one reference), each part cleaned (cleanCandidate: leading `"'[{( and trailing `"'\})], stripped), and the whole payload is a fallback when no part is valid (bare file names then count). Several references on one line are all attached.
grammar.valid: a local reference starts with `/`, `./`, `~/` (`~user` is refused), a drive or `\\`, or holds a `/` or `\` without a scheme; `../` and a `..` segment are refused; a bare `name.ext` only as the fallback. `file://` (2026.9.9 also `file:`) is stripped for the check and decoded later (trySafeFileURLToPath). http(s): only https with a public host (isAllowedRemoteMediaUrl). 2026.9.9 also takes `media://inbound/<id>` (OpenClaw's inbound media store). A `data:` URL is refused.
grammar.fences: a line inside a fenced code block is not read (2026.9.9 findCodeRegions, 2026.7.1 parseFenceSpans). Mandu reads it anyway: a fence it misread would be a bypass.
grammar.markdownImages: `![](x)` is read only on some delivery paths (extractMarkdownImages) and then only for an https URL, or a source in the allowlist of media the run's own tools produced: never a local path the model wrote
grammar.toolResults: a tool result's TEXT is not read for directives on either build: tool media come from the structured `details.media` of OpenClaw's own tools (extractToolResultMediaArtifact)
grammar.systemPrompt: 2026.9.9 system-prompt-params: "- Media attachment: own line `MEDIA:<path-or-url>` per item; path is not prose." "- Directive starts line, plain text, outside fences/Markdown; never inline or wrapped." With the message-tool-only source reply mode: "- No legacy `MEDIA:` here."

sanitizersBeforeParse.where: the reply text goes through sanitizeAssistantVisibleText / sanitizeAssistantFinalAnswerText (assistant-visible-text) and, on 2026.9.9, sanitizeUserFacingText (user-facing-text) BEFORE parseReplyDirectives: so a directive can FORM after markup inside or before it is deleted
deletes: model special tokens <|…|> / <｜…｜> (a space is put back between two letters)
reasoning tags and their content <think>, <thinking>, <thought>, <antthinking>, and <final> tags
[Tool Call: …] (with an `Arguments:` JSON after it), [Tool Result for ID …] blocks, [TOOL_CALL] blocks
plain-text tool-call blocks at a line start ([name] {json}, `commentary|analysis|final to=…`, <function=…>) up to the end of their payload
whole lines: internal trace lines, inbound metadata lines, placeholder lines
sanitizersBeforeParse.gapStart: every span deleted INSIDE a line starts with `<`, `[` or `]` (or at the line start); Mandu's ColonScan treats a colon as a possible directive when MEDIA precedes it with gaps that each start with one of those

loading.where: 2026.9.9 src/auto-reply/reply/reply-media-paths.ts createReplyMediaSourcePreparer; media/read-capability.ts resolveAgentScopedOutboundMediaAccess; media/local-roots.ts getAgentScopedMediaLocalRootsForSources
loading.absolute: read from the host. When the `read` tool is allowed (the default profile) and fs is not workspace-only, the local roots are EXPANDED with the parent directory of each named file (appendLocalMediaParentRoots), so any readable host file qualifies
loading.fileUrl: decoded by parseReplyDirectives (trySafeFileURLToPath); one that cannot be decoded is refused ("Host-local MEDIA file URLs are blocked in normal replies")
loading.types: 2026.9.9 host reads admit images, audio, video, PDF, Office documents, archives and validated plain text (.txt, csv, markdown, json, yaml): a `.env` without a known type may be refused by OpenClaw itself, a `.txt`, `.pdf` or `.zip` is not; Mandu does not rely on it
loading.store: `media://inbound/<id>` → a file of OpenClaw's inbound media store (resolveInboundMediaReference)

delivery: the embedded run's final payloads (buildEmbeddedRunPayloads → parseReplyDirectives on the final assistant text, or on every assistant text of the run when the last message has none)
a harness run's reply media (prepareHarnessReplyMedia → parseReplyDirectives)
the outbound payload normalization of every delivery (normalizeRawOutboundPayload → parseReplyDirectives), reasoning payloads excepted (shouldSuppressReasoningPayload)
block streaming: each text block as it completes (streaming-directives holds a partial `MEDIA:` line)
the gateway's auto-reply to an inbound channel message, `openclaw agent --deliver` (opts.deliver === true), heartbeat and cron runs, sub-agent completion (re-emitted as `MEDIA:` lines)
